evidence: The paper uses random forest only for imputation of missing baseline characteristics (age, sex, country via missRanger package). All substantive conclusions about drug safety signals are based on disproportionality analysis: "We used two classical disproportionality methods... the reporting odds ratio (ROR) and the information component (IC) algorithms." Five drugs consistently showing signals (methotrexate, leflunomab, sulfasalazine, rituximab, tocilizumab) are identified through ROR/IC thresholds in FAERS and VigiAccess, not through tree-based importance. Risk factors (age, sex) are analyzed via "Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses."
